text.p: Newly-merged Swiss-French employment firm Adecco SA said its total sales in the nine months of 1996 to September 30 rose 5.2 percent to 6.306 billion Swiss francs.

Sales for the third quarter alone from ordinary activities totalled 2.024 billion Swiss francs. This figure does not include results from its security and cleaning business, which was sold in September.
The firm was formed out of a merger of Swiss temporary employment firm Adia SA and French part-time employment firm Ecco SA.

Sales for the third quarter on a "pro forma" basis, calculated in the same manner as the nine-months sales, showed a rise of 6.7 percent to 2.356 billion Swiss francs, compared with the comparable 1995 quarter.

Adecco said that if the acquisition of Roevin, BCI, EcoNova, and the sale of PGA in the U.S. were omitted from results, third-quarter sales would show a rise of 8.6 percent and nine-month sales a rise of 7.8 percent.

"Against the background of the difficult economic situation in France, Germany and Switzerland, we are very satisfied with Adecco's increased turnover," said John Bowmer, Adecco's chief executive officer, in a statement.

"Currently we are concentrating fully on the merger of business activities of Adia and Ecco, in order to make full use of their synergistic potential and to strengthen the position of Adecco as a basis for further growth," Bowmer said.
